chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Abu Raja' Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said:
The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Whoever prefers any of my companions over Ali has disbelieved.

key_terms.فضل: To prefer, consider superior, give precedence to
key_terms.كفر: Disbelief (kufr), rejection of a fundamental tenet of faith

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about preferring any companion over Ali?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declared that whoever considers any of his companions to be superior to Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) has committed an act of disbelief (kufr). This hadith, narrated through Ibn Umar -- a prominent companion -- underscores the unparalleled status of Imam Ali in the Prophet's estimation. In the context of early Islamic discourse on leadership succession, this was a forceful statement asserting Ali's preeminence among all companions.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. al-Hasan al-Mu’addab narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. `Ali al-Isfahani narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Abu Raja’ Qutayba b. Sa`id narrated to us from Hammad b. Zayd from `Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj from Nafi` from Ibn `Umar. He said:
The Messenger of Allah (s) said: Whoever prefers one of my companions over `Ali has disbelieved.
